doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Wearing many hats and how Longo's big band started
summary: Longo says he knows how to finish projects, and explains how his big band formed from charts written for Dizzy's All-Star Big Band after an agent's booking request.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Good system. And you are a pianist and a band leader, and you must, to make a living in the music world you have to wear a lot of hats, right?
I do. A lot of people don’t.

They don’t have the — I guess you would say the talent for that. Or some of them are not educated that way. I used to tell my students man, education doesn’t mean you know everything in the world, it means you know how to find out. And so what I’m used to doing is being able to start a project and bring it to conclusion. Now I’ve noticed that a lot of my colleagues, they start a lot of things and they never finish them. So I’ve been doing that my whole life, I know how to finish a project.
Okay. Logistically it must be a challenge to get 15, 16, 17 players together at one time for a concert and then of course a rehearsal. Is that hard here in New York?

Well I don’t do it. The way this big band started, I was always out there with a trio after I left Dizzy, I had had my trio, which I had before I went with Dizzy. So I was teaching the guy who happened to be the lead alto player was taking lessons from me. And this agent called me up and said — I was the pianist with the Dizzy Gillespie All-Star Big Band. So the Jersey Jazz, where I played today, they wanted to hire that band. So they say, “Do you have any idea how much that costs?” I said, “Well man they were paying me a grand a concert and there’s 17 people in the band and I’m sure the leader got more money. And so she’s, “Oh man.” So I told her, I said, “I’ve got some charts that I wrote for Dizzy, that I still got them.” And I said, “I got the charts if I could get a band.” And they go, “Yeah take the gig, take the gig, I’ll get you the music. And so that’s how it started, the big band. And he got all the musicians, they were all studio cats from New York, which he
was. He was one of the top lead alto players in New York. So he put the band together. I don’t do anything but go play man and write.
All right. That’s the way to do it. You don’t have to worry about all the guys showing up.
Well they all show up, they’re all pros. My band has got the top guys in New York going in.
